title: Planning the Piece: Four Boxes Before Any Paint
objective: Plan an identity piece on the four-box planner, choosing an approved symbol, a medium, a ground and one thing you will not do, and say why each was chosen.

blocks.text: GROW · Art · Week 3. Trinity Arts Award Explore. Planning the Piece: Four Boxes Before Any Paint.
Objective: plan an identity piece on the four-box planner, choosing an approved symbol, a medium, a ground and one thing you will not do, and say why each was chosen.
Success evidence: a four-box planner filled in, with a reason under each box and a marked constraint you have agreed to keep.
Symbols come from the approved pack. The piece is about a symbol you have chosen, never about your home or family.
40 minutes. Offline.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve

blocks.text: A plan is a set of decisions, not a drawing
A plan is not a small version of the picture. A small version is just the picture, done badly.
A plan is the decisions you have made before you start: what, with what, on what, and what you will avoid.
Decisions can be argued about. A sketch can only be liked or not liked.
The fourth box is the one people skip, and it is the one that saves the piece.
It is the thing you have decided NOT to do, written down before you are tempted.
Insist on the fourth box. A planner with three boxes filled and the fourth blank is not finished.
You need the symbol pack, the medium list, the ground samples and one four-box planner.
Nothing gets made today. That is deliberate, and it is the part people find hardest.
A week between the plan and the piece is what makes the plan worth writing.

stages.data-ta1: Planners out before the symbol pack. The boxes are the lesson, not the symbols.
stages.data-ta2: If a pupil starts drawing the piece itself, take the pencil to the planner and ask for the reason under box one.

blocks.text: Two planners for the same piece
Planner A says: a bird, in paint, on paper, and it will be good.
Planner B says: the bird card, in cut paper because the edges must stay sharp, on grey card so the white shows, and no added background.
Both were written before the same lesson.
Only one of them can be checked afterwards, and only one tells you when to stop.
Planner B has already decided the hardest thing: what is not going in.
That decision is worth more than the other three put together.

items: 4 · the one thing you will not do.

blocks.text: Read planner A once more. Every word in it is true, and none of it is useful.
That is the trap: a plan can be honest and still tell you nothing.

stages.title: I Do · model

blocks.text: Filling the four boxes out loud
Box one: I take the bird card. That is my symbol and it does not change.
Box two: cut paper. I choose it because the bird's wing edges need to stay sharp.
Box three: grey card, because white cut paper on white card disappears.
Box four is the hard one. I write: no added background.
I write that because last time I filled the space around the shape and lost the shape.

blocks.caption: The fourth box is the one that stops the piece being overworked
blocks.title: The four-box planner
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: symbol, medium, ground, and the thing you will not do

blocks.text: Now the plan can be handed to somebody else and still make sense.
That is the test. If it only works because I am holding it, it is not a plan.
Say the reason under each box as you write it. The reasons are the assessed part, not the choices.
Notice I wrote box four last but thought about it first, while I chose the medium.

stages.data-ta1: Model one planner only, and make the fourth box take the longest.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits

blocks.text: Sort the boxes, match the reasons
Eight cards are on your table. Four are choices and four are reasons.
Sort them into choices and reasons first.
Then match each reason to the choice it explains.
One reason fits two choices. Say which two, and which one it fits better.
When your table is done, hold up the pair you argued about.
Hold one up even if your table did not agree; a disagreement we can see is worth having.
Two of the reason cards say almost the same thing. Decide which choice each one fits better.

stages.data-ta1: Cards sorted first. Nobody holds anything up until every table has finished.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect

blocks.text: The constraint is not a punishment
The fourth box sounds like giving something up, and it is the opposite.
A piece with no limits keeps growing until the time runs out, and then it stops wherever it happens to be.
A piece with one stated limit has a shape you can finish inside.
Choose the limit from what went wrong last time, not from what sounds hard.

boxes.head: NO LIMIT
boxes.line2: the clock decides when to stop

blocks.caption: Both pieces stop; only one of them stops on purpose
blocks.title: Working with a limit
blocks.alt: Two boxes compared: a stated limit lets the piece be finished, no limit lets the clock decide

blocks.text: Write it as a thing you will not do, not as a thing you will do carefully.
Carefully is not a limit. It is a hope.
A limit you can measure is better than one you cannot. No background is measurable.
Not too busy is not, because nobody can tell you when you have crossed it.

stages.data-ta1: Have last week's pieces available. The best fourth boxes come from looking at them.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab

blocks.text: Hand the plan over
Work in twos. Swap planners and do not explain yours.
Read your partner's four boxes and say what they are going to make.
If you cannot say it without asking a question, tell them which box was the vague one.
They fix that one box only, in words, not in a drawing.
Then swap back and do the same for theirs.
If the plan reads clearly, say so and stop. There is no mark for finding a fault.

stages.data-ta1: No talking while planners are being read. The silence is the test.

stages.title: Independent · evidence

blocks.text: Four boxes, four reasons
Work on your own. Fill all four boxes on your planner.
Write one reason under each, in a full sentence.
The fourth box says what you will not do, and why you chose that limit.
Do not start the piece. Next week is for making it, and a started piece is not a plan.
If you finish early, write one sentence saying how you will know the piece is done.

items: Supported · three boxes filled with a reason for two of them.
Standard · four boxes filled, each with a written reason.
Stretch · as Standard, and say how you will know the piece is finished.

blocks.text: Write in sentences, not single words. A single word in a box is a choice with no reason.
If you change a box, cross the old one out rather than rubbing it out; the change is evidence too.

stages.data-ta1: Scribe exact words. Do not improve a pupil's reason.
stages.data-ta2: A pupil who cannot settle on a limit may pick one from the agreed list rather than inventing one.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence

blocks.text: Read box four to an adult
Read your fourth box to the adult at your table, with its reason.
They read it back exactly and say what they think you have ruled out.
If that is not what you meant, say it again with one more word.
Then choose what happens next: keep the plan, change one box, or change the limit.
Write that choice on the planner with today's date before you leave.
The planner goes in the folder and comes out first thing next week.

stages.data-ta1: The named adult reads it back word for word without repairing it.

print.intro: Use one box per decision, with the reason underneath. Leave a box blank rather than filling it with a decision you cannot explain.
focusRows: Symbol, medium and ground, each with a written reason
One thing you will not do, decided in advance
How you will know the piece is finished
tiers: Fill three boxes and give a reason for two of them.
Fill all four boxes and write a reason under each.
As Standard, and say how you will know the piece is finished.
checks: The symbol comes from the approved pack.
Each of the four boxes carries a written reason.
The fourth box states something the pupil will NOT do.
The plan can be read by somebody else without the pupil explaining it.
